name: logseq_check_links
title: Check Links
description:
Check a [[link]] pass. ok is true only if after strips back to before, brackets balance and don't nest, every ref in before is kept, and each [[term]] names exactly one page or alias.

**Can't find:** a link to the wrong page, or a name split across a ref.

after.description: before plus [[links]], at most 500 distinct terms

name: logseq_explore_context
title: Explore Context
description:
Explore one page in a call: its blocks, related pages, and linked references (blocks that link to it, most-linking pages first). Page the references with references_offset.

**Use when:** researching a topic that has a page, or asking what links to it.
**Can't find:** topics with no page (use logseq_find_blocks), or anything past the caps (see hasMore and warnings).
**Alternatives:** logseq_get_page (content only), logseq_get_concept_network (structure only).

page.description: Page to explore (name, alias or ISO date)

max_blocks.description: Maximum number of blocks to include (default: 50)

max_related_pages.description: Maximum number of related pages to include (default: 10)

max_references.description: Maximum number of reference blocks to include (default: 20)

references_offset.description: Reference blocks to skip, most-linking pages first (default: 0)

include_temporal_context.description: Include temporal context for journal pages (default: true)

format.description: json (default), or markdown text. Markdown has block uuids only on search hits and with compact

compact.description: Block snippets and uuids, no bodies. Read one with logseq_get_block

name: logseq_find_blocks
title: Find Blocks
description:
Find blocks, newest first. Filters AND (one or more): text (substring, case-insensitive); page; links_to (1-5 pages; [[x]] or #x, not plain text); property + value (exact); period on journals (start_date + end_date, last_n days or preset). Pages by limit (max 500) and offset: check hasMore.

**Can't find:** synonyms, stems, ranged values, or how pages connect (logseq_search_by_relationship).

text.description: Text to find in block content (case-insensitive, literal)

page.description: Only blocks on this page and its aliases (page name, alias or ISO date)

links_to.description: Only blocks that link to every one of these pages, under any of their names: [[x]], #x and #[[x]] count, plain text does not (1 to 5 page names, aliases or ISO dates)

property.description: Block property to match (letters, digits, "-" and "_"; createdAt and created-at are equivalent). Needs value

value.description: Exact value of the property. A multi-value property matches if any one value equals it. Needs property

start_date.description: Start date in YYYYMMDD format (e.g., 20251115). Needs end_date

end_date.description: End date in YYYYMMDD format (e.g., 20251120). Needs start_date

last_n.description: Only blocks on journal pages in the last N calendar days, today included (whole number, 1+)

preset.description: Named period in local time; weeks run Monday to Sunday

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 100, max: 500)

offset.description: Results to skip, newest first; shifts if the graph changes

slim_results.description: Slim blocks (default). false returns full entities

name: logseq_find_pages
title: Find Pages
description:
Find non-journal pages as { name, aliases? }. Filters AND: text (substring of name or alias); names (up to 50, exact name or alias; each answered with its page, or null plus closest names); property + value (page property).

**Can't find:** journals (logseq_query_by_date_range), block text (logseq_find_blocks), or past 200 (use offset). Warning pages_unavailable: list unknown, not empty.

text.description: Filter pages whose name or alias contains this text (case-insensitive)

names.description: Page names or aliases to look up exactly, ignoring case (1 to 50)

property.description: Page property to match (letters, digits, "-" and "_"; createdAt and created-at are equivalent). Needs value

value.description: Exact value of the property. A multi-value property matches if any one value equals it. Needs property

offset.description: Pages to skip, in name order; shifts if the graph changes

format.description: json (default), or toon text: a list's keys once, not on every row

name: logseq_get_block
title: Get Block
description:
Get one block by UUID, optionally with its children. UUIDs come from other results and from ((uuid)) refs in content.

**Can't find:** blocks by text (logseq_find_blocks) or by numeric id. For a whole page use logseq_get_page.

uuid.description: UUID of the block to retrieve

format.description: json (default), or markdown text. Markdown has block uuids only on search hits and with compact

name: logseq_get_concept_evolution
title: Get Concept Evolution
description:
Track a concept over time: blocks on its page and blocks linking to it, grouped by day, week or month, with optional date bounds.

**Use when:** "how has X evolved?" or "what's the history of Y?"
**Can't find:** unlinked plain-text mentions (logseq_find_blocks), topics with no page, or dated mentions past 500 (narrow dates).
**Alternatives:** logseq_query_by_date_range for plain journal queries.

concept_name.description: Concept to track (page name, alias or ISO date)

start_date.description: Optional start date in YYYYMMDD format

end_date.description: Optional end date in YYYYMMDD format

name: logseq_get_concept_network
title: Get Concept Network
description:
Map pages linked to a concept as nodes and edges, in both link directions, up to max_depth hops. One edge per page pair, with a reference count.

**Caps:** 50 pages, 15 new per page; journal pages are shown but not expanded. If truncated is true, raise max_nodes/max_fanout or set expand_journals.
**Can't find:** unlinked pages, or what pages say (logseq_explore_context).

concept_name.description: Root concept (page name, alias or ISO date)

max_nodes.description: Maximum pages in the network, root included (default: 50, max: 500)

max_fanout.description: Maximum new pages any one page may add (default: 15, max: 100)

expand_journals.description: Expand through journal pages instead of treating them as leaves (default: false). Journal pages link to almost everything, so this can flood the network.

format.description: json (default), or markdown text. Markdown has block uuids only on search hits and with compact

name: logseq_get_current
title: Get Current Context
description:
Get what the user is looking at in LogSeq right now: the open page, the block being edited, and any selected blocks.

**Use when:** the user says "this page", "this block" or "what I'm looking at" without naming it. Then pass the page name to logseq_explore_context or logseq_get_page.

**Can't find:** anything not open right now. Returns page: null with a message when no page is open.

name: logseq_get_graph
title: Get Graph Info
description:
Get the connected graph's name and filesystem path.

**Use when:** confirming which graph is attached or debugging paths.
**Can't find:** anything about content. See logseq_find_pages and logseq_explore_context.

name: logseq_get_page
title: Get Page
description:
Get a page by name (case-insensitive). detail: page (default), full (adds its blocks) or outline (top-level blocks: uuid, first line, child count).

**Use when:** you know the page name.
**Can't find:** pages by keyword (logseq_find_blocks, logseq_find_pages).
**Alternatives:** logseq_explore_context adds related pages and what links here.

page.description: Page name, alias, or ISO date (2025-01-01) for a journal

detail.description: page (default): the page itself. full: adds its blocks, nested. outline: top-level blocks as uuid, first line and child count

resolve_refs.description: Add resolvedContent/resolvedRefs for ((uuid)) refs and {{embed}}s (depth 2). Not for outline

format.description: json (default). markdown for page and full, toon for outline

name: logseq_query_by_date_range
title: Query by Date Range
description:
Query journal entries by start_date + end_date, last_n journals, or a preset (give exactly one), with optional search.

**Use when:** "what did I do last week?" or catching up. summary.topConcepts shows what a period was about.
**Can't find:** non-journal pages, days with no journal, or blocks past 200 (max_blocks, max 1000).
**Alternatives:** logseq_get_concept_evolution, logseq_find_blocks.

start_date.description: Start date in YYYYMMDD format (e.g., 20251115). Needs end_date

end_date.description: End date in YYYYMMDD format (e.g., 20251120). Needs start_date

last_n.description: The N most recent journals that exist (whole number, 1+), newest first

preset.description: Named period in local time; weeks run Monday to Sunday

search_term.description: Optional search term to filter blocks

slim_results.description: Slim blocks (default). false returns full entities

include_content.description: false returns only per-day block counts and top-level snippets

top_concepts_limit.description: Entries in summary.topConcepts, the most-linked pages (default 10). 0 omits it

max_blocks.description: Max blocks across all days, nested ones counted (top-level with include_content false), default 200, max 1000

name: logseq_search_by_relationship
title: Search by Relationship
description:
Find whether topic A connects to topic B within max_distance link hops (connected-within, the only type). If so, returns the blocks of both pages. Both topics must be pages. Capped by limit (max 500): see warnings.

**Can't find:** blocks that link to a page (logseq_find_blocks links_to), plain-text relationships, or over 500 results.
**Alternatives:** logseq_get_concept_network (overview).

topic_a.description: Primary topic to search for (page name, alias or ISO date)

topic_b.description: Related topic that defines the relationship (page name, alias or ISO date)

relationship_type.description: Type of relationship: connected-within (topics connected within N hops), the only one. Blocks that link to a page: logseq_find_blocks with links_to

limit.description: Max results (default: 50, max: 500). connected-within counts every block of both pages, nested ones too, topic A's first; a block that lost children has childrenTruncated
